notes: Moon and Mars site parameters grounded in NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO Diviner) south pole data and Curiosity REMS / Perseverance MEDA Jezero Crater measurements, scaled for playable mission sessions.

moon.name: Moon · Shackleton Crater
moon.subtitle: Lunar South Pole Rim (89.5°S)
moon.skyDescription: Pitch-black airless sky with Earth gleaming above the horizon.
moon.dustNote: Electrostatic lunar regolith dust clings to seals and solar panels, cutting efficiency unless cleaned.
moon.dataSourceName: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Diviner & LOLA
moon.imageCredit: NASA / GSFC / Arizona State University (LRO LROC Shackleton Crater mosaic reference)
moon.realVsSimplifiedNote: True lunar day+night is ~29.5 Earth days (14d sunlight / 14d dark at equatorial/mid-latitudes; Shackleton rim peaks get ~80% sun). Modeled as 14 sols sunlight + 14 sols night (or shortened cycle in Lunar Night scenario) so solar vs battery/RTG trade-offs shine.

mars.name: Mars · Jezero Crater
mars.subtitle: Ancient Lakebed Delta (18.4°N)
mars.skyDescription: Butterscotch dusty atmosphere with Phobos drifting overhead.
mars.dustNote: Global and regional dust storms can dim Martian sunlight for days or weeks!
mars.dataSourceName: NASA Perseverance MEDA & Curiosity REMS Weather Stations
mars.imageCredit: NASA / JPL-Caltech / MSSS (Jezero Crater Perseverance reference)
mars.realVsSimplifiedNote: Real Mars sol is 24h 39m 35s and Curiosity RAD measured ~0.67 mSv/day surface radiation. Earth-Mars one-way light time varies 3 to 22 minutes; animated in seconds during gameplay so kids experience delayed Mission Control replies without waiting 20 real minutes.
